questions.prompt: Before configuring a custom Okta SAML integration, an engineer has only the application's marketing name. What information is most useful next?

options.text: The application's supported SAML requirements for the exact environment.
options.explanation: Endpoints, identifiers, protection and identity output need an authoritative integration contract.

options.text: Any ACS copied from an unrelated working app.
options.explanation: A working value elsewhere does not establish this application's receiving address.

options.text: An arbitrary issuer string chosen for convenience.
options.explanation: The actual provider relationship determines approved issuer information.

options.text: A private signing key requested from the application vendor.
options.explanation: Collecting another party's private signing key is not the normal metadata exchange.

questions.prompt: An approved Atlas ACS is https://atlas.example/saml/acs. What job does this value identify?

options.text: The application's receiving location for the selected SAML sign-in response.
options.explanation: The ACS is a receiving endpoint, distinct from the SP's identity and resource pages.

options.text: The user's employee identifier.
options.explanation: A subject identifier does not name the response endpoint.

options.text: The signing certificate fingerprint.
options.explanation: A key fingerprint does not identify a message-delivery address.

options.text: A guarantee of successful application access.
options.explanation: Delivery to the ACS still requires acceptance and application decisions.

questions.prompt: Atlas's entity ID is https://atlas.example/saml and its ACS ends in /saml/acs. Which should represent Atlas as the intended assertion audience in this agreement?

options.text: The approved SP entity ID.
options.explanation: Audience identifies the relying party; it is not selected merely by resembling an endpoint.

options.text: Any URL beginning with the same hostname.
options.explanation: A shared host does not make different identifier values interchangeable.

options.text: The browser's current page URL automatically.
options.explanation: Resource navigation and the agreed audience have different purposes.

options.text: The user's email address.
options.explanation: The subject's identifier does not identify the intended SP audience.

questions.prompt: An SP entity ID resembles an HTTPS address. What must be true for its identity role?

options.text: Its exact value must agree with the integration's expected participant identity.
options.explanation: An entity identifier is not necessarily an address a browser must retrieve successfully.

options.text: Opening it must always display the sign-in page.
options.explanation: Participant identity does not require that exact value to host a sign-in page.

options.text: It must equal the ACS in every application.
options.explanation: Participant identity and message delivery can have different values.

options.text: It must contain the employee's name.
options.explanation: An SP identity is not a user identifier.

questions.prompt: Atlas test has a different ACS and entity ID from production. What is the sound configuration approach?

options.text: Use the approved test values and the intended test trust relationship.
options.explanation: Environment boundaries should remain explicit even when applications look similar.

options.text: Copy production endpoints because the software is the same.
options.explanation: Identical software does not merge test and production identity or routing.

options.text: Change only the visible integration label.
options.explanation: A label change does not change actual targets, issuer or trust.

options.text: Accept responses intended for either environment without distinction.
options.explanation: That would discard the supplied target separation.

questions.prompt: A metadata document contains SPSSODescriptor. What does that element describe?

options.text: The entity's service-provider SSO role and its advertised configuration.
options.explanation: The role descriptor carries SP-related declarations; it is not a user's authentication result.

options.text: A specific user passing authentication.
options.explanation: Metadata describes participants and capabilities, not a completed user attempt.

options.text: An Okta session cookie.
options.explanation: A role descriptor is XML configuration information, not browser session state.

options.text: The application's authorization decision for a page.
options.explanation: Resource decisions require application processing evidence.

questions.prompt: Metadata advertises an endpoint with a Location and a Binding URI. Why should they be read together?

options.text: The address and delivery mechanism jointly describe the advertised endpoint.
options.explanation: An endpoint's address alone does not identify how a message must be carried.

options.text: The binding replaces the need for an address.
options.explanation: A delivery mechanism still needs an appropriate destination.

options.text: The Location determines every permitted signing algorithm.
options.explanation: Endpoint location does not by itself define the full algorithm policy.

options.text: The browser may ignore either value whenever authentication succeeds.
options.explanation: Authentication does not authorize arbitrary delivery behavior.

questions.prompt: An application receives the provider's public signing certificate. What is its intended use?

options.text: Verification under the application's approved issuer/key trust rules.
options.explanation: Public verification material helps check signatures but needs an authorized trust relationship.

options.text: Producing signatures as the provider without another key.
options.explanation: Signing requires the corresponding private-key capability.

options.text: Decrypting every assertion encrypted to the application.
options.explanation: Recipient decryption uses the application's corresponding private capability, not the provider's public signing certificate.

options.text: Proving the user has the administrator role.
options.explanation: Key material alone does not establish resource authorization.

questions.prompt: A downloaded XML metadata file is well formed. What is still needed before adopting its keys?

options.text: An approved basis for authenticating and trusting the metadata source.
options.explanation: Readable XML is not proof that its configuration is authorized for this integration.

options.text: Nothing, because XML syntax establishes trust.
options.explanation: Syntax validation and source authenticity are separate questions.

options.text: A matching fingerprint copied from that same unverified download.
options.explanation: Self-consistency is not independent authentication of the source.

options.text: Permission to trust any later replacement from any location.
options.explanation: Trust adoption must remain scoped to the approved process.

questions.prompt: An SP advertises WantAssertionsSigned=true. What does that declaration establish by itself?

options.text: The advertised expectation that assertions be signed.
options.explanation: The declaration still needs supported sender configuration and actual receiver enforcement.

options.text: That every received assertion signature has already verified.
options.explanation: Metadata is not a verification result for a particular message.

options.text: That the SP signs its outgoing AuthnRequests.
options.explanation: Outgoing request signing is a different responsibility.

options.text: That assertion encryption is mandatory.
options.explanation: Signing expectations do not automatically require encryption.

questions.prompt: An SP advertises AuthnRequestsSigned=true. Which responsibility does this concern?

options.text: The SP's authentication requests being signed.
options.explanation: It describes outgoing request behavior, distinct from the IdP's response protection.

options.text: The IdP encrypting every response.
options.explanation: Encryption is a different mechanism and direction.

options.text: The application checking projects permission.
options.explanation: Resource authorization is not a request-signing declaration.

options.text: The browser creating an approved provider signature.
options.explanation: A browser carrying a request does not become the provider's signer.

questions.prompt: Metadata advertises a NameID format, but an integration has no agreed source for the actual value. What is missing?

options.text: The identity source and application matching agreement.
options.explanation: A format declaration does not select the emitted value or establish the account relationship.

options.text: Only the color of the login button.
options.explanation: Appearance cannot resolve identity output.

options.text: A rule that NameID must always be email.
options.explanation: NameID value and semantics depend on the agreed integration.

options.text: A guarantee that the attribute is a private key.
options.explanation: An identity format does not make the subject value cryptographic secret material.

questions.prompt: SP metadata requests department. What proves department was actually supplied in a sign-in?

options.text: Inspection of the relevant emitted assertion and application interpretation.
options.explanation: A requested claim and its observed release are different evidence.

options.text: The request declaration alone.
options.explanation: An advertised request does not establish the provider's actual output.

options.text: A successful browser redirect to the IdP.
options.explanation: Redirect delivery says nothing about released department values.

options.text: The application containing a department column.
options.explanation: Local storage capability does not prove the assertion included the claim.

questions.prompt: Metadata has validUntil=12:00 UTC. At exactly 12:00, what does this deadline mean?

options.text: The metadata has reached its validity limit.
options.explanation: validUntil is an expiry boundary; reaching it is not merely a refresh suggestion.

options.text: It starts a new application session automatically.
options.explanation: Metadata expiry does not create application state.

options.text: It remains valid indefinitely if a prior signature verified.
options.explanation: A valid signature does not remove the metadata validity bound.

options.text: It expires only when the user closes the browser.
options.explanation: This deadline concerns configuration metadata, not a browser lifetime.

questions.prompt: A metadata cacheDuration has elapsed, with no validUntil expiry or other invalidity established. What follows from cache age alone?

options.text: A refresh-related threshold has been reached, not automatic metadata invalidity.
options.explanation: Caching and strict validity are separate; actual use still follows applicable implementation and deployment policy.

options.text: Every established app session must end immediately.
options.explanation: Metadata cache age does not define every application session lifetime.

options.text: The cached metadata must be trusted without source checks.
options.explanation: Source authentication remains necessary regardless of cache age.

options.text: The metadata's signature must have become mathematically invalid.
options.explanation: Cache age does not alter the signed XML's mathematical verification by itself.

questions.prompt: A metadata parent expires at 16:00 and a child at 15:00. What is the child's effective maximum validity from those bounds?

options.explanation: A child can impose a shorter limit; it cannot extend the applicable parent limit.

options.text: 16:00 because the longer time always wins.
options.explanation: The shorter applicable expiry constrains the child.

options.text: 17:00 after adding the two deadlines.
options.explanation: Expiry instants are not additive durations.

options.text: No expiry because two values cancel each other.
options.explanation: Multiple applicable limits do not erase each other.

questions.prompt: A standalone root EntityDescriptor omits both validUntil and cacheDuration. A generic schema parser accepts it. Which conclusion is sound?

options.text: Schema success alone does not establish the metadata root rule was met.
options.explanation: The metadata specification requires at least one root freshness attribute despite their individual schema optionality.

options.text: Schema success proves complete protocol conformance.
options.explanation: A schema does not encode every specification or deployment requirement.

options.text: The root automatically inherits an expiry from an absent parent.
options.explanation: A standalone root has no supplied parent limit to inherit.

options.text: The omitted attributes are application passwords.
options.explanation: They concern metadata freshness and validity, not credentials.

questions.prompt: Okta publishes a new signing certificate in metadata. What establishes that Atlas can use it?

options.text: Approved effective receiver trust and verification evidence for the intended new key.
options.explanation: Publication is not the same operation as receiver adoption and runtime verification.

options.text: The new certificate merely appearing on a setup page.
options.explanation: Availability does not establish the receiver's effective configuration.

options.text: A successful old-key attempt on an unrelated receiver.
options.explanation: That observation does not test new-key adoption at Atlas.

options.text: Changing the integration's display name.
options.explanation: A label change does not install verification material.

questions.prompt: A catalog integration exists for an app, but a project requires a specific supported feature. What should determine suitability?

options.text: The exact integration's documented capabilities and requirements.
options.explanation: Catalog presence is a starting point, not proof that every desired feature is supported.

options.text: The icon looking identical to a production icon.
options.explanation: Branding is not a capability contract.

options.text: An assumption that custom always means more secure.
options.explanation: Security depends on the supported configuration and controls, not that label alone.

options.text: An assumption that all SAML capabilities are included.
options.explanation: A protocol-defined option is not automatically a product feature.

questions.prompt: Which handover best supports maintaining an Okta-to-Atlas integration?

options.text: A record of authoritative values, owners, trust sources and refresh/change behavior.
options.explanation: Another engineer needs both current agreement and responsibility for keeping it effective.

options.text: Only a screenshot saying login worked.
options.explanation: A screenshot omits configuration provenance, limits and ownership.

options.text: A copy of every user's password.
options.explanation: Passwords are not required handover material for this federation relationship.

options.text: Only the public product names.
options.explanation: Names alone do not identify the specific environment or effective configuration.
